# History Rewrite (November 26, 2026)

On November 26, 2026, every branch was rewritten with `git filter-repo --replace-text` to remove private details that had been committed to this public repository. Only the redacted strings changed in file contents, and each rewritten branch has the same number of commits. Authors and dates are unchanged. Two side effects of `git filter-repo`: it dropped the GPG signatures GitHub had added to its web-merge commits (so they no longer show as Verified), and it rewrote abbreviated SHAs inside 8 commit messages to point at the new commits.

## What was replaced

| Detail | Placeholder |
| --- | --- |
| AWS account ID (including inside the S3 bucket name) | `REDACTED-ACCOUNT-ID` |
| AWS support case number | `REDACTED-SUPPORT-CASE` |
| Elastic IP address | `REDACTED-IP` |
| VPC endpoint ID | `REDACTED-VPC-ENDPOINT` |
| EC2 instance IDs | `REDACTED-INSTANCE-ID` |
| EBS volume IDs | `REDACTED-VOLUME-ID` |
| Local home directory | `~` |
| Local user name | `REDACTED-USER` |
| Name of an unrelated project | `Project B` |

The placeholders are uppercase on purpose. Uppercase is not allowed in S3 bucket names, so a redacted bucket name can never resolve to a bucket someone else creates.

Code, workflows and the checked-in September recovery manifest now carry the placeholder bucket name. GitHub Actions reads the real AWS identifiers from repository secrets, `EDGER_AWS_ROLE_ARN`, `EDGER_CORPUS_STORE` and `EDGER_S3_BUCKET`, so the runner masks them in logs. Every `configure-aws-credentials` step also sets `mask-aws-account-id: true`. Local runs that need the real bucket pass it through `EDGER_CORPUS_STORE`, `EDGER_CAMPAIGN_INPUT_URI` or `--campaign-uri`. Re-running the completed September scaling recovery would also need the real bucket put back into the recovery manifest and `scripts/edger-scaling-recovery.mjs`.

## Commit SHAs

Every commit SHA changed. Text written before the rewrite cites the old SHAs. That includes SHAs pinned inside hashed evidence, which were deliberately left as they were: `RECOVERY_SOURCE_SHA` (`f25a4880…`), and the c3 lineage commit `567ec98` recorded in the promoted policy, its report and `src/ai/generated/edgerPolicyCurrent.js`. Use the map below to translate an old SHA to its rewritten commit. The original history is kept only in a private local backup.
